headline: Australian home sales hit 16-year low as prices soar
summary: October home sales fell to the lowest level since the Great Recession, with buyers retreating amid 7 % mortgage rates and all-time high property prices, marking a sharp slowdown in the market.

headline: Florida St Patrick’s Day parade cancelled after anti-DEI law
summary: Delray Beach announced the cancellation of its popular St Patrick’s Day parade to comply with a new Florida law that bars municipalities from hosting events deemed to promote diversity, equity and inclusion, sparking public outrage.

headline: Gunman kills one and injures four in Washington DC shooting
summary: A shooter opened fire near the White House, killing a person at a gym and wounding four others. Police later contained the suspect, who shot himself. The incident shifted from an active-shooter response to a barricaded-subject operation, with authorities urging residents to stay indoors.

headline: US bill proposes Medicare eligibility at age 50
summary: Legislation under consideration would lower the Medicare eligibility age from 65 to 50, extending coverage to about 60 million American workers. The proposal, distinct from Medicare-for-All, aims to broaden health security for mid-career adults.

headline: Disney partners with Cosm to bring Star Wars to dome theatres
summary: Cosm secured a multi-year film deal with Disney, bringing "Star Wars: A New Hope" and future titles to its dome venues as part of a broader collaboration.

headline: European leaders reject Russian push to overhaul continent’s security
summary: EU heads pushed back against Moscow’s proposal to revamp European security structures, with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy warning of heightened risks as talks continue in Abu Dhabi.

headline: Nebius shares tumble 16% after weak 2026 capex outlook
summary: Nebius fell 16 % on the market after issuing a cautious outlook for 2026 capital expenditure, lagging behind peers IREN and CoreWeave that posted stronger recent results.

headline: MSF says millions of Ebola aid funds missing, staff unpaid
summary: Médecins Sans Frontières warned that large sums of Ebola relief money are unaccounted for, leaving medical staff without pay, training or essential supplies as the virus continues to spread.

headline: Employer-backed home purchases rise as housing affordability worsens
summary: A MarketWatch survey notes an increase in first-time buyers receiving financial assistance from their employers, highlighting the growing difficulty of purchasing a home even for those with stable jobs.

headline: Oil prices mixed after Trump says Iran deal not needed
summary: Crude futures moved sideways on Thursday following President Donald Trump’s comments that a U.S.–Iran agreement was unnecessary, sparking concerns the conflict could continue.

headline: Mortgage rates 7% in 1997, but housing costs now higher proportion of income
summary: A CNBC analysis shows that although mortgage rates were 7 % in 1997, today’s typical home consumes a much larger share of household earnings, making home buying feel more expensive despite similar rates.

headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid scandal
summary: Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia chief executive after an affair with an employee alleged to be a Chinese spy. Shares fell up to 10%, wiping tens of billions from market value. Colette Kress was named interim CEO and Huang’s $140 billion stake, held jointly with his wife, adds uncertainty.

headline: Farage appears on Russell Brand podcast, criticises Labour
summary: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage featured on Russell Brand’s US podcast, condemning the Labour party for “cosying up” to the comedian after Brand’s recent sexual-assault conviction.

headline: UK health agency warns low meningitis B vaccine uptake among teens
summary: UKHSA says only 28% of 18- and 19-year-olds have received the first dose in a one-off campaign, amid an outbreak that caused three deaths and serious illness.

headline: Mississippi’s last black senators before Scott Colom highlighted
summary: The piece recalls the two black men who served as US senators from Mississippi before Scott Colom, the first black senator from the state since 1874.

headline: Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico over illegal immigration
summary: President Trump says levies will increase if Mexico does not curb illegal crossings, signalling a possible escalation in trade tensions.

headline: Two men convicted of aiding Iran in plot against UK journalists
summary: Men of Iranian origin were found guilty of conducting surveillance for Tehran’s intelligence services to facilitate violence against UK-based journalists between 2024 and 2025.

headline: Australian federal police warn of surge in teen extremist material
summary: AFP says 32 of 37 youths prosecuted for extremist offences were charged in the past two years, with many found possessing “hard drives full of gore”.

headline: New allegations emerge against convicted rapist Ralph Carr
summary: Former staffers detail unwanted sexual advances by Melbourne talent manager Ralph Carr, who was previously found guilty of raping an ex-employee.

headline: NSW ICAC report highlights ‘guns for hire’ issue, calls for reform
summary: The corruption watchdog’s inquiry reveals ease of undeclared lobbying and gun-for-hire problems, criticising both major parties for inaction on recommended reforms.

headline: NSW Labor runs 'news' Instagram account, raising communication law concerns
summary: A new Instagram account presenting itself as an independent news source is being operated by the NSW Labor party. Experts warn it exploits a loophole in political communication rules, as the state government and other parties also use similar unaffiliated accounts to share partisan content.

headline: Poundland granted two-week extension to secure buyer
summary: UK discount retailer Poundland has received a high-court order extending its creditor protection by two weeks while it seeks a new owner. The move gives the chain, which employs about 12,000 staff, more time to evaluate bids from three potential purchasers.

headline: UK proposes ending criminal record checks for youth offences
summary: The government plans to stop requiring employers to see criminal records of people convicted of offences committed under the age of 18. Ministers say the change will help reduce youth incarceration and improve employment prospects for disadvantaged young people in England and Wales.

headline: Record credit-card balances raise risk of hidden medical-debt
summary: U.S. consumers have pushed credit-card debt to a new high, and experts warn that mounting medical bills are increasingly being added to cards, creating “shadow debt” that is harder to track and could strain household finances.

headline: Zimbabwe author cleared after AI plagiarism probe
summary: Simbarashe Kundizeza has been exonerated following a month-long investigation that confirmed his Caine prize-winning short story was written by a human, ending allegations that artificial intelligence was used.

headline: Unions claim credit for Democratic wins in 2026 midterms
summary: Labor unions say their multi-million-dollar spending and member mobilisation helped Democrats secure major victories in the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, and are now urging the party to deliver concrete policy actions.

headline: UK economy outperforms expectations amid AI boost
summary: Analysts note that the UK has posted its fastest growth in over two years, driven in part by artificial-intelligence adoption. Despite concerns over a tech slowdown and rising energy costs, the economy expanded by 0.7% in the latest quarter, defying earlier forecasts.

headline: Ukraine power plant operates under constant drone threat
summary: One of Ukraine’s largest power stations, heavily damaged by a Russian missile strike, remains functional but faces ongoing danger from drone attacks, highlighting the precarious state of the country’s energy infrastructure.

headline: Australian quantum start-up Q-CTRL reaches unicorn status
summary: Q-CTRL, a home-grown quantum-technology company, has been valued at over $1 billion after raising $420 million, expanding its portfolio from quantum-software tools to a navigation system developed with Airbus.

headline: Petrol prices fall as global oil costs drop 20%
summary: Australian motorists are seeing lower pump prices after crude oil prices slipped by about one-fifth this month, providing temporary relief for drivers facing high fuel expenses.

headline: Metro Bank puts itself up for sale, billionaire eyes £420m windfall
summary: Metro Bank announced it is seeking bids after three years since its rescue, with Colombian billionaire Jaime Gilinski Bacal expected to reap a £420 million gain if the sale proceeds, sending the share price up 7%.

headline: Bomb hoax threats trigger evacuations at Italian schools
summary: Schools across Italy faced fresh evacuations after receiving bomb threats for a second consecutive day, causing panic among students and staff.

headline: OECD reports migration to rich countries falls for second year
summary: The OECD says inflows to wealthy nations declined for a second year as stricter visa rules limit workers, students and refugees moving abroad.

headline: Meta restores Australian Femicide Watch page
summary: Meta has reinstated the Femicide Watch page that tracks murders of women in Australia after founder Sherele Moody requested its revival.

headline: Milburn review proposes cuts to youth welfare benefits in UK
summary: Former Labour minister Alan Milburn's review recommends reducing welfare payments for young people not in education, employment or training. The proposal could represent the biggest overhaul of the UK benefits system in a decade, aiming to address rising numbers of NEETs and reshape the welfare landscape.

headline: Manchester United dismiss Carrick as manager
summary: Manchester United have sacked former midfielder Michael Carrick after a ten-month tenure that left the club in the relegation zone. The club said a change was necessary to achieve its ambitions for the season.

headline: Former DJ Tim Westwood denies additional sexual offence charges
summary: Ex-Radio 1 presenter Tim Westwood appeared in court to deny two further sexual offence charges, bringing the total to 17 alleged offences spanning 1983 to 2016. He entered not-guilty pleas for all charges.

headline: Far-right activist admits damaging Channel dinghy
summary: Daniel Thomas, a far-right activist, changed his plea to guilty on a single charge of criminal damage after slashing a dinghy with a knife in the Channel. He continues to deny a separate charge of failing to disclose a phone PIN to police.

headline: Strategist warns against chasing tech stock bounce
summary: Jim Thorne, chief market strategist at Wellington-Altus Private Wealth, cautioned investors not to be lured into a rapid rebound in tech stocks, describing the potential bounce as "violent" but urging restraint until fundamentals improve.

headline: Scout Motors nears completion of South Carolina plant with 212,000 reservations
summary: Scout Motors reported roughly 212,000 reservations for its Terra pickup and Traveler SUV as its $2 billion manufacturing facility in South Carolina approaches completion, signalling strong consumer interest ahead of the vehicle launch.

headline: Burberry posts profit as sales surge in China and US
summary: Luxury fashion house Burberry returned to profit, driven by a 6% sales increase across coats, jackets and handbags. Strong online and wholesale performance in China and the United States underpinned the growth, which CEO Joshua Schulman credited to a back-to-basics strategy.

headline: Israeli strike hits Gaza's Nasser hospital, killing six
summary: An Israeli missile struck Nasser hospital in Khan Younis, Gaza, killing six people including a surgeon and a disabled man, and wounding more than 20. The health ministry said the building housed surgical wards and intensive care units. Israel said it targeted Hamas fighters but offered no evidence.

headline: Ukraine reports Starshield satellite disruptions amid US-Russia talks
summary: Ukraine's president said recent speed restrictions on the Starshield military satellite network were hindering its defence efforts. The concerns were raised as US envoys arrived in Moscow for talks with President Putin, highlighting tensions over the technology's reliability in the ongoing conflict.

headline: Euclid mission maps 900 million galaxies in first data release
summary: The European Space Agency’s Euclid telescope released its inaugural dataset, revealing more than 900 million galaxies and about 15,000 gravitational-lensing candidates. The mission aims to produce the largest three-dimensional map of the universe, covering a third of the sky and tracing cosmic history back over 10 billion years.

headline: College students rally across US campuses to back Starbucks boycott
summary: Students, staff and elected officials gathered at more than 40 US colleges to support the Starbucks Workers United boycott. The campaign seeks higher pay, a $17-hour minimum wage and a three-person staffing minimum, after five years of stalled contract talks with the coffee chain.

headline: John Kerry calls Trump ‘biggest loser’ over climate policy at COP31
summary: Speaking at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey, former US secretary of state John Kerry criticised former President Donald Trump for withdrawing the United States from climate commitments and handing the clean-energy lead to China, saying the move makes Trump the biggest loser in the climate arena.

headline: NHS England removes claim that 137 trusts benefit from Palantir AI
summary: After The Guardian exposed that only 29 NHS trusts were using Palantir’s AI data platform, NHS England deleted a website statement that had claimed 137 trusts were benefiting from the technology, acknowledging the earlier information was misleading.

headline: Maga architects blame Big Tech and AI data centres for US midterms loss
summary: The Heritage Foundation’s head argued that the Republican Party’s embrace of Silicon Valley and the fallout from the US-Iran war contributed to their defeat in the recent midterm elections, linking tech-sector policies to voter backlash.

headline: Ukraine says Starlink restrictions reinstated as US envoys arrive in Moscow
summary: Ukraine reported that restrictions on SpaceX’s Starlink service have been re-imposed, coinciding with a visit by US officials to Moscow. The move follows heightened tensions over Russian drone activity and diplomatic talks involving senior US figures.

headline: Greta Thunberg criticises Australia’s net-zero progress at COP31
summary: At the COP31 summit in Turkey, climate activist Greta Thunberg slammed Australia’s pace on net-zero emissions, describing it as slower than a snail. Her remarks drew a large media presence and prompted security guards to escort her from the stage.

headline: The return of the snatch-and-grab state
summary: A new historical analysis examines how modern governments employ confiscation tactics as a form of economic warfare, reviving the concept of the snatch-and-grab state in contemporary policy debates.

headline: Anti-AI trade measures boost Indian equities, analysts say
summary: Research suggests that the worst anti-AI trade policies by major chipmakers correlate with stronger performance of Indian stocks, highlighting a potential investment angle as global tech regulation intensifies.

headline: Italy proposes exit tax on emigrants’ capital gains
summary: The Italian government has introduced a tax targeting capital gains of wealthy emigrants, aiming to capture revenue from assets moved abroad. While theoretically sound, officials acknowledge challenges in practical implementation.

headline: Floreat gunman’s recording revealed at inquest into murders
summary: During the inquest into the deaths of Jennifer and Gretl Petelcyzc, evidence emerged that the Floreat shooter inadvertently recorded himself on the day of the attack, shedding new light on his interactions with police prior to the incident.

headline: Australia to spend $80m on workforce for AUKUS
summary: The Australian government will allocate more than $80 million to expand training pathways and build a skilled workforce capable of supporting the AUKUS defence partnership, aiming to attract workers at all career stages and boost domestic capability for the submarine project.

headline: UK drone maker UForce valued at £4.5bn after £500m fundraise
summary: London-based naval drone company UForce, founded by Ukrainian entrepreneurs, reached a £4.5 billion valuation after raising over £500 million, including a £113 million investment from the UK’s national wealth fund, making it one of the country’s fastest-growing unicorns with equipment used extensively in the Ukraine war.

headline: Government provider breach may have exposed personal details
summary: A government-run service provider disclosed that a cyber breach could have compromised personal information, including contact details, of individuals whose data it holds, prompting an investigation and advice for affected users to monitor for potential misuse.

headline: Italy’s anti-vax doctors seek return to frontline amid political push
summary: A group of Italian doctors stripped of their licences for anti-vaccination views are lobbying for reinstatement, with support from far-right politician Roberto Vannacci, as the debate intensifies ahead of the 2027 elections and raises questions about medical staffing and public health policy.

headline: 72-year-old British woman missing from cruise ship in Atlantic
summary: A 72-year-old British passenger vanished from the Tui cruise liner as it sailed towards the Caribbean, prompting a search operation by authorities and the cruise line while family members appeal for information on her whereabouts.

headline: Mayoral candidates propose reforms to curb council toxicity
summary: Candidates vying for mayoral office have suggested measures such as reducing council representatives, appointing an external auditor and tightening meeting discipline to address reports of a toxic, bullying culture within the local council and restore public confidence.

headline: Prince Harry and Meghan settle in new Cotswolds home
summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have moved into a new residence on a friend’s estate in the Cotswolds, following their return to the United Kingdom with their children earlier this year, according to reports.

headline: Senator Cotton urges US ban on Chinese memory chip maker CXMT
summary: US Senator Tom Cotton has called on the Commerce Department to place Chinese DRAM producer CXMT on the Entity List, citing national-security concerns as the company expands its memory-chip production and moves into high-bandwidth memory markets.

headline: Ex-bureaucrat says minister likely struck CFMEU deal over complaint line
summary: A former senior public servant testified to a Queensland inquiry that the former minister probably reached an agreement with the construction union CFMEU concerning a complaint-handling line, describing the arrangement as a logical conclusion to the regulator’s backtrack on union-friendly policies.

headline: Labuschagne’s aggressive batting fuels call for Webster’s recall
summary: Former Australian all-rounder believes Labuschagne’s energetic performance with the ball could trigger a resurgence and support a recall for veteran spinner Webster.

headline: Social-media app seen as key voter influencer in Ringwood
summary: The Chinese-Australian community in Melbourne’s east holds considerable voting power, urging politicians to recognise its diversity and long memory ahead of the Victorian election.

headline: Ukrainian drone startup UFORCE valued at $6 billion
summary: UFORCE, a defence-tech startup, reached a $6 billion valuation as investors back its battle-tested drones and naval vessels that have logged hundreds of thousands of combat flights.

headline: Liberal party urges big business to look after itself
summary: Liberal MP Tim Wilson told big firms they must fend for themselves, arguing the Coalition still owes small businesses for its handling of the pandemic.

headline: Coalition lacks climate policy as debate shifts
summary: The opposition argues the Coalition has moved from a developed climate policy to none, while Labor claims it is on the right side of history.

headline: Universities face domestic caps, urged to cut overseas fee reliance
summary: Tertiary education chief Barney Glover warned universities they must secure futures without depending on lucrative international student fees after domestic enrolment caps are imposed.

headline: Community opposition to data-centre expansion cited as democratic pushback
summary: Advocates say data centres will keep NSW at the technological forefront, but local residents argue the boom should not come at the expense of their suburbs.

headline: Sam Konstas scores century, pressures NSW Test selectors
summary: Konstas’s latest hundred for New South Wales in the Sheffield Shield puts Test selectors under pressure to consider him for the national side.

headline: Bikie gang violence targets Brighton property developer
summary: A violent campaign by a bikie gang against developer Simon Pitard resulted in an innocent couple being caught in the crossfire at their Cheltenham home.

headline: Storm damage forces school closures across Brisbane
summary: Several schools were shut after storms damaged facilities, with authorities warning that more severe weather is expected in the coming days.

headline: Large beetles spotted in Brisbane suburbs, authenticity questioned
summary: Residents reported seeing huge beetles around Brisbane, though experts suggest many may be imposters rather than the iconic Christmas beetle.

headline: Hervey Bay woman sets Guinness record with turtle collection
summary: A local woman earned a Guinness World Record after amassing thousands of turtle and tortoise collectibles, becoming the first to achieve the feat.

headline: Pat Cummins faces crucial test of captaincy ahead of Friday match
summary: Australia’s Test captain Pat Cummins, who has led the side for 15 years, approaches a pivotal moment as his leadership will be judged in the upcoming Friday game, with expectations to deliver under pressure.

headline: US journalist Evan Gershkovich swapped after Russian espionage conviction
summary: After being detained by Russia’s FSB in Yekaterinburg, US reporter Evan Gershkovich spent months in a Russian jail before being exchanged for an assassin in a prisoner swap, highlighting the complexities of espionage cases between Moscow and Washington.

headline: Mitch Marsh defends straight-bat approach amid Sandpapergate questioning
summary: Australian cricketer Mitch Marsh responded firmly to media queries linking him to the 2018 South Africa tour controversy, emphasizing his commitment to a straight-bat style and refusing to be drawn into past scandals.

headline: Tasmania urges visitors to ‘stay away’ in tongue-in-cheek campaign
summary: Tourism Tasmania launched a provocative marketing drive telling Australians the island “is not really for tourists”, using former SBS presenter Lee Lin Chin to suggest travellers prefer the label “traveller” over “tourist”, aiming to reshape visitor perception.

headline: Ball-tampering bans hit Smith, Warner and Bancroft financially and reputationally
summary: Former Australian cricketers Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft face lasting damage from the 2018 sand-paper scandal, with losses measured in both reputation and multi-million-dollar earnings, prompting debate over possible remedies.

headline: UK economy posts fastest growth in over two years
summary: The United Kingdom recorded a 0.7% expansion in the three months to September, the strongest quarterly increase since early 2022, according to official data. The growth was driven by a rebound in services and consumer spending, narrowing the gap with the European average.

headline: Ukrainians endure blackouts as Russian attacks hit power grid
summary: Families in Ukraine face daily life disruptions with limited electricity, water and heating after Russian strikes target the national power network, leaving many households coping with only a few hours of power each day.

headline: Atlassian finds AI-trained graduates can outpace some managers
summary: Atlassian’s chief AI enablement officer reports that recent graduates using artificial intelligence tools performed better than certain senior managers in tests, highlighting the technology’s potential to accelerate experience and reshape workplace roles.

headline: Inquiry finds falling house prices haven’t improved affordability
summary: A parliamentary inquiry revealed that despite recent declines in house prices, affordability has worsened due to supply shortages, with banks questioned on profits and forecasts suggesting prices may continue falling until 2028.

headline: Four Ugandan schoolgirls die after suspected orange poisoning
summary: Four girls at a Ugandan school fell ill and died after eating oranges brought by a classmate, prompting police to investigate the source of the fruit and the circumstances of the suspected poisoning.

headline: Football Australia seeks alternative venue as Socceroos wary of Jordan
summary: Socceroos players have expressed reluctance to travel to Jordan over security concerns, prompting Football Australia to look for a different location for upcoming fixtures.

headline: US Treasury yields climb ahead of inflation and housing data
summary: US Treasury yields edged higher as bond markets reopened after Veterans Day, with investors awaiting fresh inflation and housing figures for further direction.

headline: AustralianSuper reprimands IFM over exotic travel junkets
summary: AustralianSuper has issued a formal reprimand to IFM Investors, accusing the fund manager of excessive overseas travel and demanding tighter controls on staff trips linked to its airport holdings.

headline: New Zealand duo win men's and women's Golden Boot awards
summary: Ponga and Waaka secured the men's and women's Golden Boot awards respectively after delivering standout performances in their respective leagues.

headline: ANZ and Westpac warn mortgage pressure will worsen
summary: Chief executives of ANZ and Westpac told parliament that rising interest rates are only starting to bite household budgets and that mortgage stress is set to increase before any relief is felt.

headline: Cartoonist David Rowe releases November 2026 political cartoons
summary: Multiple Walkley-award winner David Rowe publishes his November 2026 political cartoons, continuing his daily commentary in the Chanticleer column.

headline: Prime Minister's golf grant sparks demand for honorary Albo memberships
summary: Bar staff at the historic nine-hole course on the Cooks River report a surge in calls from locals asking for honorary "Albo" memberships after the PM's grant became public.

headline: Ex-wife of police prosecutor delivers victim impact statement after C-section
summary: The ex-wife of a police prosecutor gave a powerful victim impact statement in court following his conviction for a series of domestic-violence offences, speaking shortly after giving birth via C-section.

headline: New owner reopens Bowen Basin coal mine employing 275 workers
summary: A Queensland firm has purchased and restarted a fourth Bowen Basin coal mine, bringing back 275 jobs despite previous owners deeming the operation unprofitable due to royalty costs.

headline: Morgan Stanley's StraitNZ unit attracts multiple bidders in Rothschild auction
summary: At least two firms have submitted proposals for Morgan Stanley's $1 billion StraitNZ business as the Rothschild-run auction reaches its final stage. The sale could reshape the regional banking landscape and draw significant interest from investors seeking exposure to New Zealand markets.

headline: Coronial inquest into nine-year-old drowning delayed as new evidence emerges
summary: A coronial inquest into the death of a nine-year-old boy who drowned has been adjourned after fresh evidence, including Triple Zero call recordings, was presented in court. The delay allows further investigation into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy.

headline: Queensland Labor apologises for policy inflating building costs by 20%
summary: Queensland Labor has issued an apology for a policy that added extra pay for rainy days and halted work in hot weather, effectively raising building costs by about 20%. The measure, tied to CFMEU enterprise agreement conditions on government tenders, sparked criticism from the construction sector.

headline: One Nation warns Victoria establishment in heated parliamentary speech
summary: One Nation leader Warren Pickering delivered a forceful speech in Victoria, warning the state's establishment and delivering a pointed performance during the question-and-answer session. The remarks underscored the party's opposition to the current government and highlighted growing political tensions in the state.

headline: Gas bills set to rise about 5% from Dec 1 amid Middle East turmoil
summary: Island Energy announced that gas bills will increase by roughly 5% from 1 December as ongoing instability in the Middle East continues to pressure global energy markets. The hike will affect households and businesses, adding to cost-of-living concerns across the region.

headline: Capability X surges 50% on ASX debut
summary: Capability X jumped almost 50% to close at 29c on its ASX debut, raising $12 million to expand its industrial safety technology. The strong performance came despite weak IPO conditions and global AI stock jitters, marking a notable entry for the new tech firm.

headline: Auric Mining secures $17m to expand WA gold projects
summary: Auric Mining has locked in $17 million to accelerate its gold growth strategy in Western Australia. The funding will support drilling at the Munda, Union Jack and newly acquired Iron Maiden projects, bolstering the company's expansion plans in the region.

headline: Indonesia's vice-president resigns amid impeachment calls
summary: Indonesia's vice-president has resigned following mounting calls for his impeachment. The resignation follows political pressure and controversy, leaving the position vacant and prompting speculation about potential successors and the impact on the country's leadership.

headline: NSW teacher banned after taking intimate images of sleeping man
summary: NSW teacher Brody Luke Anderson has been banned from working in any public school after taking photographs of a naked sleeping man. The disciplinary action follows an investigation into the inappropriate conduct, though the teacher avoided jail time.

headline: Albanese's announcements eclipsed by coffee cart and embassy post
summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's recent announcements struggled for attention as a coffee cart and a viral Instagram post from the Finnish embassy gained more traction. Critics and rumours further diluted the impact of the government's messaging ahead of upcoming summits.

headline: Queensland searches for heir to historic 16m × 60cm land strip
summary: The Department of Transport and Main Roads is seeking the long-lost owner of a narrow 16-metre by 60-centimetre land strip in south-east Queensland. The parcel last belonged to 19th-century businessman August Thorsborne, who died over a century ago.

headline: Police investigate sudden death in Kuranda
summary: Police responded to a residence in Kuranda just before 10:30 am and found a man deceased. Officers are now investigating the circumstances surrounding the sudden death, with details yet to be released.

headline: Court hears alleged murderer threatened victim after breakup
summary: In a Melbourne court, prosecutors said Lamarre-Condon sent a message to alleged murder victim Jesse Baird stating he would not exist following their breakup. The exchange was presented as evidence of intimidation during the trial.

headline: Russian diesel exports double after US lifts sanctions
summary: Russian diesel shipments are set to double following the removal of US sanctions, according to the Financial Times. Analysts warn the surge may be short-lived as Ukraine resumes attacks on Russian refineries, potentially curbing export volumes.

headline: France backs Spain's candidate for ECB presidency
summary: Paris and Berlin have signalled support for Pablo Hernández de Cos, Spain’s nominee for the European Central Bank presidency, aiming to create a package deal on central-bank leadership across the eurozone.

headline: Lawyer seeks reduced sentence for drug trafficker's driver
summary: In an Australian court, counsel argued that Stephen Roche, an Irish national who pleaded guilty to attempting to pervert the course of justice, should receive a lighter jail term for his role in helping a fugitive drug trafficker evade authorities.

headline: Suburbs where house prices have surged up to 417% listed
summary: SBS News compiled a list of Australian suburbs where house prices have risen dramatically, with some areas seeing increases of more than four-fold over the past 15 years, highlighting stark regional disparities in property growth.

headline: Indigenous-owned observatory opens in remote South Australia
summary: A new observatory, owned and operated by an Indigenous community in South Australia’s far west, has opened to showcase ancient star stories and promote cultural tourism, according to ABC News.

headline: Democrats celebrate first Black Mississippi senator since 1874
summary: The historic election of a Black senator from Mississippi, the first since former slave Blanche Bruce in 1874, was hailed by Democratic leaders as a milestone for representation and progress.

headline: Tasmanian rock lobster fisheries closed over antibiotic trade risk
summary: Parts of Tasmania’s south-east commercial rock lobster and dive fisheries will be shut for three months to mitigate trade risks linked to antibiotic use in the salmon industry, the ABC reports.

headline: Jury hears texts from husband on day his wife died
summary: During a trial, the jury was shown months of text messages between Robert Crawford and his wife, including a message sent on the day she died, providing insight into their relationship before the fatal incident.

headline: Flagship Minerals secures option on Chilean copper-gold project
summary: Flagship Minerals announced it has obtained an option over the Fortuna Valle copper-gold project in Chile’s Coquimbo region, citing extensive historic drill hits across the district-scale resource.

headline: ANZ chief warns of dangerous global market situation
summary: ANZ CEO Nuno Matos told reporters that rising interest rates and frothy equity markets have created a "dangerous situation" for global investors, urging caution as financial conditions tighten.

headline: Suppliers see potential upside from David Jones store closures
summary: Some suppliers believe that the planned closure of several David Jones stores could boost sales by concentrating shoppers into fewer, higher-performing locations, according to ABC News.

headline: Parramatta releases Addo-Carr to join new club
summary: Parramatta has decided not to extend Josh Addo-Carr’s contract beyond next season, allowing the winger to leave the Eels and sign with another NRL club immediately if he chooses.

headline: Alternative assets dominate single-family office portfolios
summary: Alternative investments now make up 60% of single-family office holdings, overtaking traditional assets for the first time, according to BNY Wealth, reflecting a shift among the world’s super-rich toward non-conventional assets.

headline: Royal commission questions redactions in Andrews government documents
summary: The inquiry into the Victorian state’s response to the pandemic has raised concerns over extensive redactions and omissions in communications involving former premier Daniel Andrews and his top adviser, demanding further evidence.

headline: NSW community preschools warn funding model could cut staff ratios
summary: Preschool operators in New South Wales say the state’s new funding formula, which increases child numbers while reducing staff, may undermine care quality and safety, prompting a united opposition from the sector.

headline: Debate intensifies over Social Security’s long-term solvency in US
summary: Analysts warn that demographic trends could strain Social Security, while Senator Bernie Sanders proposes ending the taxable earnings cap to increase contributions from high-income earners and keep the programme solvent for future generations.

headline: Pat Cummins to address Khawaja allegations in media briefing
summary: Australian Test captain Pat Cummins confirmed he will hold a press conference in Sydney to respond to recent claims involving former player Usman Khawaja, following a week of public discussion about past ball-tampering incidents.

headline: Victorian opposition leader Jess Wilson shares dream dinner guests and policy priorities
summary: In a rapid-fire interview, Jess Wilson, leader of the Victorian Opposition, revealed the people she would invite to a fantasy dinner and highlighted the key policy reforms she sees as most urgent for the state.

headline: Historic SS United States sunk off Florida to become artificial reef
summary: The former trans-Atlantic liner SS United States, once the fastest ocean liner, was deliberately sunk off Destin, Florida, where it will serve as the world’s largest artificial reef, ending its 70-year maritime career.

headline: Former Trump officials relocate to US military bases over security concerns
summary: Several senior figures from the Trump administration, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, have moved onto military installations citing heightened security threats, sparking discussion about protection for former officials.

headline: Data-centre firm NextDC sued over alleged unpaid commissions
summary: Australian data-centre operator NextDC is facing a lawsuit from a former sales manager who claims the company owes him millions of dollars in commissions, adding pressure to the fast-growing firm.

headline: Oil slicks from Gulf ship strikes threaten marine life
summary: Hundreds of oil spills have been recorded in the Strait of Hormuz since the US-Iran conflict began, creating large slicks visible from space. The spills have spread across the Gulf, contaminating coastlines and endangering dolphins, sea turtles and fish in the region’s fragile ecosystems.

headline: APRA to conduct AI stress test on banks and super funds
summary: APRA chief John Lonsdale warned that major Australian banks and superannuation funds are not adequately prepared for AI-driven cyber threats and announced a landmark stress test to assess their resilience.

headline: Parliament questions PM Albanese’s $6m golf grant claim
